blocks.text: Foreground mode attaches to stdout/stderr and proxies signals to PID 1; `-d` returns immediately; `-i` keeps STDIN open; `-t` allocates a TTY; `--rm` deletes the container on exit.

rows: Ctrl-C sends SIGINT to PID 1; if PID 1 ignores it, nothing happens
Deletes logs and inspect state on exit

blocks.text:
$ docker exec -i db psql -U app rag < seed.sql        # -i only: correct for pipes
$ docker exec -t db pg_dump -Fc rag > dump            # BROKEN: TTY corrupts binary output
$ docker attach worker                                # PID 1's stdio, not a new shell

items: Detach from an attached `-it` session without stopping it: Ctrl-P, Ctrl-Q.
`exit` in a shell that is PID 1 stops the container.
Without a TTY, Python block-buffers stdout: set `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`.

blocks.text: `-t` in CI fails with "the input device is not a TTY", merges stderr into stdout and converts `\n` to `\r\n`. Use `-i` alone, or `-T` in Compose.

Q: "When do you use -i vs -t?" A: "-i when data is piped into the container's stdin; -t only for an interactive terminal. Never -t for scripts or binary output, because the TTY rewrites line endings and merges streams."

items: attach = PID 1's stdio; exec = new process.
